tree.title: the taxonomy
tree.description: A node is {id, label: {en, tr}, how?, picto?, children?}; leaves have no children and wear the picture named by `picto` (default: their id: combination, meta, augmentation, cascade, weighted, switching, mixed); `how` is a one-line "how it combines" under the name (the flat form). The widget checks the nested nodes (the schema subset cannot recurse); one to three levels under the root.

grow.title: one press per entry
grow.description: The node ids that grow in each press. Every node but the root exactly once; a node grows in a press after the one of its parent, or in the SAME press when its parent is listed before it (then it grows from the top down, `chainMs` after the parent).

highlight.title: leaves emphasised in the last press
highlight.description: Leaf ids. The route from the root and a ring on the nodes mark them. An empty list drops the last press.

link.title: the dotted line
link.description: A dotted line from node `from` (a leaf) to node `to`, drawn when `from` grows. An empty `from` draws none.

linkNote.title: what the dotted line means

default.en: Dotted: feature augmentation counts as monolithic when the next recommender has to be adapted.
default.tr: Noktalı çizgi: sonraki öneri sistemi uyarlanacaksa özellik artırma monolitik sayılır.

linkNote.description: Shortened from the site's hybrid.taxonomy.dotted.tip. Empty `en` shows no note.

figureLabel.title: the text alternative of the whole figure

default.en: The taxonomy of hybrid systems as a tree. Hybrid systems split into monolithic, ensembles and mixed. Monolithic holds feature combination and meta-level. Ensembles split into sequential (feature augmentation, cascade) and parallel (weighted, switching). A dotted line joins monolithic to feature augmentation.
default.tr: Hibrit sistemlerin ağaç olarak taksonomisi. Hibrit sistemler monolitik, topluluklar ve karma olarak ayrılır. Monolitik; özellik birleştirme ve meta-düzeyi içerir. Topluluklar ardışık (özellik artırma, kademeli) ve paralel (ağırlıklı, geçişli) olarak ayrılır. Noktalı bir çizgi monolitiği özellik artırmaya bağlar.

tree-grow.steps: Each press grows one branch of the tree (default: the three families, the monolithic leaves, the two ensemble branches, the sequential leaves with the dotted line, the parallel leaves); the last press, when `highlight` names leaves, draws the route to them and rings them.

mode.title: what the table shows
mode.description: blend: the weighted blend (rows, columns, the sum). matrix: a schematic rating matrix and what each recommender sees of it. mnar: the same matrix, its gaps are not random. pseudo: a content-based model fills the empty cells of a sparse matrix with pseudo-ratings, the collaborative model reads it, and the weight of a pair of users grows with their real ratings. Every mode takes four presses.

matrix.title: the matrix modes (mode matrix and mnar)

cells.title: the observed cells, row by row (users)
cells.description: One string per user, one character per film: "." is an empty cell, "1".."5" an observed rating (its level shows only in mnar mode). All strings the same length, 3..7. The new film (a column) and the new user (a row) are added by the widget, empty.

held.title: the held-out cells, "row:column" (mnar mode, press 2)
held.description: Each must be an observed cell.

labels.title: the short labels of the pictures

pseudo.title: the pseudo-rating mode (mode pseudo)
pseudo.description: `real` and `fill` are one string per user, one character per film: "." empty, "1".."5" a rating. `fill` has a pseudo-rating exactly where `real` is empty. `read` are the two users compared in press 3 (row numbers from 0). `pairs` are the numbers of REAL ratings of the two users of a pair (press 4); `full` is the number from which a user's weight is full.

full.tr: her biri {n}+ gerçek puan: tam ağırlık
her biri {n}+ gerçek puan: tam ağırlık

labels.title: the short labels of the picture
labels.description: `full` may hold {n}: the number from which a weight is full.

default.tr: her biri {n}+ gerçek puan: tam ağırlık

groups.title: the groups mode (mode groups)
groups.description: `labels` name the three groups of inputs, the model, its output and the film card (`{n}` is replaced by `filmRatings`, how many ratings the few-ratings film has: an example, the card carries no label, D-129).

rows.title: the base recommenders
rows.description: One row each: {label: {en, tr}, icon?, prediction (0..5 stars), weight}. icon is one of users, items, matrix, tag, flame, user, funnel, magnifier, eye, eyeoff, clipboard, ratings, attributes, sliders, screen, bucket, target, coverage, diversity, novelty, longtail. The product and the sums are computed. The numbers are an example; the speaker note and the evidence record say so (D-129: a picture that is plainly an example carries no label).

negativeNote.title: note on the first negative weight

default.en: Negative weight: the blend moves away from this recommender
default.tr: Negatif ağırlık: karışım bu önericiden uzaklaşır

badge.title: the tag on the film poster
badge.description: The story: a newly released film. Empty `en` shows no tag.

emblem.title: the emblem on the poster (a generic shape; no real film)

table-highlight.steps: Four presses in every mode. blend: the base recommenders' predictions for the new film (stars and numbers), their weights (bars; a negative weight leans left and is marked), the products, then the products travel into the sum, the total lands and fills the film's stars. matrix: what the collaborative, the content-based and the knowledge-based recommender each see of a rating matrix, then their three blind spots together. mnar: the observed ratings pile up high, the held-out ratings come from the same selection, the screen outside the matrix was never measured, accuracy is not the only measure. pseudo (WP-50): the real ratings of a sparse matrix, the pseudo-ratings of a content-based model fill every empty cell, the filled vectors of two users side by side with an arc of similar taste, then the weight multipliers of three pairs of users (a bar that grows with their real ratings and is full from `full` of them; the counts are shown, the bars carry no number). groups (WP-50): the three groups of inputs (ids, film content, user profile), one model that reads them all, its predicted rating, a film with only two ratings (synthetic) for which the box of the ids dims and the film content lights up, then the three arrows washed in gold together.

mode.title: what the pipeline shows
mode.description: cascade: films pass a rough first recommender and a second one that only settles ties (six presses). switch: a switch at the entrance and two ways, chosen by how many ratings the user has or by a measurement (four presses). designs: the two designs of an ensemble of recommenders, parallel and sequential, as boxes and arrows ending in a combiner, and the designs of the taxonomy that belong to each (three presses). kinds: what an ensemble reads, one kind of data into three different models or two kinds of data into two models, both into a weighted blend, the weights of the second coming forward (three presses). meta: a content-based model learns a profile for each user, the collaborative model compares users by these profiles, then feature augmentation (an output is handed on) against meta-level (the model itself is) (three presses).

models.title: the bucket of models and their errors (synthetic)
models.description: Each {id, train, held}: the error on the ratings the model was fitted on, and on held-out ratings (0..1.2, lower is better). The lowest training error and the lowest held-out error must belong to different models: that is the pair the last press shows.

labels.title: the short labels of the pictures

designs.title: the designs mode (mode designs)
designs.description: The labels of the boxes and the two panels, and the two chips under each panel (the designs of the taxonomy that belong to it: one design belongs to one panel).

kinds.title: the data-kinds mode (mode kinds)
kinds.description: The labels of the picture: the two panel titles, the two kinds of data, the five models, the blend and the prediction (the picture shows no data value, so it has no note about being schematic or synthetic). The three models of the homogeneous panel must be different models.

meta.title: the meta-level mode (mode meta)
meta.description: The labels of the picture and the bars of the three profile cards. The second and the third card are the two similar profiles (the pill between them says so), so their bars must be closer to each other than to the first card's. The bars are an example (no label on the picture, D-129).

profiles.title: the bars of the three profile cards
profiles.description: Each card: three numbers 0..1 (comedy, drama, sci-fi), the length of the bars. An example, no number is written.

items.title: the candidates, in arrival order
items.description: Each {id, coarse, fine?}: `coarse` is the first recommender's rough score (1..5, equal scores tie), `fine` the second one's score, needed for every kept item that ties.

cut.title: the first recommender keeps the items scoring at least this

ratings.title: the ratings of the user in the story
ratings.description: The story: a new user who has rated only a few films (each 1..5 stars, drawn as a small poster with its stars). An empty list draws no user.

verdict.title: the last press: what stage 2 did and did not do
verdict.description: Each {ok, text}: ok draws a check (positive), otherwise a cross (negative). They appear one by one, after the evidence.

pipeline.steps: cascade mode, six presses: the candidates appear, the first recommender ranks them roughly (many tie), it cuts the weakest, the ties are bracketed and the second recommender scores only them, it orders each tie inside its group, then the verdict (same groups, the single item stayed put, cut items do not return). switch mode, four presses: a new user (three ratings) is switched to the content-based way, a user with a long history to the collaborative way, the bucket of models picks the winner by held-out error, then wrong (by training error) next to right (by held-out error). designs mode, three presses: the parallel design (an input, two recommenders side by side, a combiner, a prediction), the sequential design (a chain that ends in the same combiner, with two dashed arrows that may also be there: the original input to the next recommender and the earlier output to the combiner), then two chips under each panel naming the designs of the taxonomy that belong to it, in the order of the tree. kinds mode, three presses: the homogeneous panel (one box of data, three different models, a weighted blend, a prediction), the heterogeneous panel (two boxes of data of two kinds, a collaborative and a content-based model, the same blend; the upper panel goes quiet), then the weights of the lower panel come forward (the two arrows into the blend drawn again, thicker, with the labels w1 and w2). meta mode, three presses: the content-based model learns a profile (one card, a user and three bars), two more users and the pill that joins the two alike profiles while the collaborative model reads the three, then two rows, feature augmentation (an output, a rating, is handed on) above meta-level (the model itself is).

mode.title: what is compared
mode.description: lists: two recommenders' lists side by side (three presses). families: the three families of ensembles, bagging, boosting and stacking, one schematic picture each, and their counterparts for rating matrices (four presses).

families.title: the families mode (mode families)
families.description: `data` are the markers of the data; `resamples` one string of markers per resample (letters of `data`, a letter may come twice or not at all: sampling with replacement); `predictions` one synthetic number per resample (their mean is shown); `wrong` the examples (0..examples-1) the first and the second boosted model get wrong; `cells` the ratings resampled in the matrix picture ("row:film" in a 5 x 6 matrix, one may come twice).

compare.steps: lists mode, three presses: a long-history user's home page shows two lists side by side (content-based and collaborative); the newly released film appears only in the content-based list (the collaborative list has an empty place); nothing is merged, the user reads both. families mode, four presses (WP-50): bagging (three resamples of the data with replacement, each into a model, three synthetic predictions averaged), boosting (a chain of three models, the examples a model gets wrong ringed and grown for the next, a weighted vote), stacking (three base models, their predictions as columns, a second-level learner, one prediction), and the same ideas for rating matrices (resampled ratings, k of 2k neighbours, two random starts of a factorization); every picture is schematic.

mode.title: the picture
mode.description: vote: the chance that the majority of n members is right, for independent members, for copies of one model and (optional) for members that are right less than half of the time, beside the number line of Galton's village fair, and a bar of squared bias + variance + noise in invented proportions, tagged synthetic data (seven presses). milestones: the published test RMSEs of the Netflix Prize as ordered milestones with a target line, the Grand Prize tie, and a separate card of production numbers (four presses).

galton.title: Galton's village fair
galton.description: The number line of the left panel: the scale (`min` .. `max`), the true (dressed) weight, the middle of the guesses, how many usable guesses there were, the unit, and the labels. The percentage is worked out from the two weights.

xTicks.title: the numbers of members written under the axis

independent.title: independent members
independent.description: `points` are [n, chance] pairs in rising n, from the deck's script. `shown` are the n of the first press (the curve is drawn up to the last of them, the rest in the second); `labelled` are the n whose value is written.

label.en: Independent members, each right 75% of the time
label.tr: Bağımsız üyeler, her biri zamanın %75'inde doğru

default.en: Independent members, each right 75% of the time
default.tr: Bağımsız üyeler, her biri zamanın %75'inde doğru

copies.title: copies of one model
copies.description: Copies of one model are right or wrong together, so the majority is as right as the one model: a flat dashed line. `points` as above.

worse.title: members that are right less than half of the time (optional press)
worse.description: Empty `points` drops the press. `tag` says who chose the number ("chosen by us").

label.en: Members right only 40% of the time

default.en: Members right only 40% of the time

decomposition.title: the three parts of the expected error (invented proportions)
decomposition.description: `parts` are the bar's segments left to right with a share of the bar each (an invented proportion, not a number of the lecture); `total` names the whole; `synthetic` is the tag that says the proportions are invented (D-127).

default.en: A chart of the chance that the majority of a committee is right. Independent members, each right 75% of the time, give 75% for one member, 89.65% for five, 95.11% for nine and 98.76% for seventeen. Copies of one model stay at 75%. Members right only 40% of the time make the committee worse. Beside it, Galton's village fair: the middle of 787 guesses, 1207 pounds, was within 1% of the ox's dressed weight, 1198 pounds.
default.tr: Bir kurulun çoğunluğunun doğru olma olasılığının grafiği. Her biri zamanın %75'inde doğru olan bağımsız üyeler, bir üye için %75, beş üye için %89,65, dokuz üye için %95,11 ve on yedi üye için %98,76 verir. Bir modelin kopyaları %75'te kalır. Zamanın yalnız %40'ında doğru olan üyeler kurulu daha kötü yapar. Yanında Galton'ın köy panayırı: 787 tahminin ortancası, 1207 libre, öküzün karkas ağırlığının, 1198 librenin, %1'in içindeydi.

milestones.description: The published test RMSEs of the Netflix Prize as ordered milestones, a target line, the Grand Prize tie, and a separate card of production numbers.

xTitle.en: Milestones in order, not drawn to a time scale
xTitle.tr: Kilometre taşları sırayla, zaman ölçeğine göre çizilmedi

figureLabel.en: A chart of published test RMSE values of the Netflix Prize, lower is better, with the milestones in order. Cinematch scored 0.9525 on the test set (0.9514 on the quiz set). The 2007 Progress Prize reached 0.8723 and the 2008 Progress Prize 0.8627. The Grand Prize ended in a tie at 0.8567 on 26 July 2009 between BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos (18:18:28) and The Ensemble (18:38:22); the earlier submission won. The target was 0.8572, 10% better than Cinematch. Beside the chart, a card of three numbers Netflix gave for what ran in production: SVD 0.8914, RBM 0.8990 and their linear blend 0.88, with the set not stated.
figureLabel.tr: Netflix Ödülü'nün yayımlanmış test RMSE değerlerinin grafiği; düşük olan iyidir, kilometre taşları sırayla. Cinematch test kümesinde 0,9525 aldı (quiz kümesinde 0,9514). 2007 İlerleme Ödülü 0,8723'e, 2008 İlerleme Ödülü 0,8627'ye ulaştı. Büyük Ödül, 26 Temmuz 2009'da BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos (18:18:28) ile The Ensemble (18:38:22) arasında 0,8567'de beraberlikle bitti; önce gönderilen kazandı. Hedef, Cinematch'ten %10 iyi olan 0,8572'ydi. Grafiğin yanında Netflix'in üretimde çalışan şey için verdiği üç sayının kartı: SVD 0,8914, RBM 0,8990 ve doğrusal karışımları 0,88; hangi kümede ölçüldükleri belirtilmemiş.

chart-draw.steps: Mode milestones, four presses: 1 the published test RMSE of Cinematch with its line, the target line (10 per cent better) and the bracket between them; 2 the progress prizes of 2007 and 2008 and the Grand Prize come one after the other on a ladder of milestones (not a time axis), the Grand Prize is a tie of two teams at the same height with their submission times, the earlier submission won; 3 the leaderboard dims and a card of its own shows what ran in production (three numbers, set not stated); 4 both are washed in gold together. Mode vote, seven presses (six without the worse curve): 1 the village fair of Galton (the dressed weight of an ox and the middle of 787 guesses on a number line); 2 the chance that the majority is right for independent members, each right 75 % of the time, at n = 1 and 5; 3 the rest of the curve (n = 9 and 17 written); 4 copies of one model: a flat dashed line, no gain; 5 members that are right only 40 % of the time: the vote gets worse (optional, empty `worse.points` drops it); 6 the chart dims for a bar of squared bias + variance + noise in invented proportions (tagged synthetic data); 7 the chart returns and the gap between the independent curve and the flat line is washed in gold.
